blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A global cash flow strategy, properly designed, is both a defensive instrument and an offensive one. Defensively, it protects the business from funding shocks, from regulatory changes that freeze money in particular jurisdictions, and from the silent drag of idle balances scattered across the group. Offensively, it funds opportunistic investment, supports acquisitions with internal firepower, and gives the board the courage to move quickly when competitors cannot.

Having measured the net position of the group, the strategy begins with trapped cash — balances sitting in countries where they cannot easily be moved. For each pool, the question is not whether it can be freed, but at what cost, and whether that cost is worth paying now or later.

Built into all of this is the habit of thinking in scenarios. What does the cash picture look like in a normal quarter, a stressed quarter, a crisis? A strategy that only works when everything goes to plan is not a strategy — it is a wish. The best global treasurers know the difference, and structure their work to hold up in the second and third pictures as well as the first.

items.q: According to the text, a well-designed global cash flow strategy is…
options: both a defensive and an offensive instrument
an accounting exercise with no strategic value
items.why: "is both a defensive instrument and an offensive one" — o texto abre exatamente com essa dupla natureza.

items.q: On the offensive side, what does the strategy give the board?
options: the courage to move quickly when competitors cannot
items.why: "gives the board the courage to move quickly when competitors cannot" — está no lado ofensivo.

items.q: What does the strategy focus on FIRST, after measuring the net position?
items.why: "the strategy begins with trapped cash — balances sitting in countries where they cannot easily be moved."

items.q: The author suggests that the real question about trapped cash is…
options: at what cost it can be freed, and whether that cost is worth paying
who is to blame for it
how to hide it from regulators
items.why: Inferência: "the question is not whether it can be freed, but at what cost" — o foco desloca-se para o preço e o timing.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Scenario thinking is central to good treasury work.
Idle balances quietly drag on performance.
A plan that only holds up when everything goes to plan is still a solid strategy.
items.why: Inferência: "A strategy that only works when everything goes to plan is not a strategy — it is a wish." O autor rejeita frontalmente essa ideia.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando a revisão da estratégia de caixa ao comitê executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. Before I take you through the numbers, let me be blunt about where the group actually stands on cash. On paper, we are comfortable. In practice, roughly a third of what the consolidated balance shows is trapped — sitting in three jurisdictions where exchange controls make repatriation slow, expensive, or both.

So the headline figure flatters us. If a funding shock hit next quarter, we could not simply reach for that money. That is the gap between the net position on the slide and the cash we can actually deploy.

What I want the committee to take away today is not a single plan, but a way of thinking. I have modelled three pictures: a normal quarter, a stressed quarter, and an outright crisis. In the normal case, the idle balances are merely inefficient. In the stressed case, they become a genuine constraint on our firepower for acquisitions. In the crisis case, they are the difference between acting and freezing.

My recommendation is that we begin releasing two of the trapped pools now, while the cost of doing so is manageable, rather than waiting until we are forced to pay a premium under pressure.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Sophie, why does the consolidated balance overstate the group's real position?
options: the numbers were calculated in the wrong currency
roughly a third of the reported cash is trapped
half of it has already been spent
items.why: "roughly a third of what the consolidated balance shows is trapped."

items.q: What makes the cash in those three jurisdictions hard to move?
options: poor forecasting by the local teams
an internal freeze imposed by the board
exchange controls that make repatriation slow, expensive, or both
items.why: "three jurisdictions where exchange controls make repatriation slow, expensive, or both."

items.q: What does Sophie say she wants the committee to take away?
options: a way of thinking, based on three scenarios
a decision to stop all acquisitions
items.why: "not a single plan, but a way of thinking" — ela modela três cenários.

items.q: When Sophie says "the headline figure flatters us," she implies that…
options: the real deployable cash is lower than the figure suggests
the group has outperformed its rivals
the number should be reported more prominently
items.why: Inferência: 'flatters us' = o número parece melhor do que a realidade; o caixa realmente utilizável é menor.

items.q: Why does Sophie recommend releasing two trapped pools NOW rather than later?
options: because the board has already approved the spend
because interest rates are about to rise
because the cost of doing so is manageable now, versus a premium under pressure later
because the local regulators have set a deadline
items.why: Inferência: "while the cost of doing so is manageable, rather than waiting until we are forced to pay a premium under pressure."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Nearly half of the group's cash is trapped cash, stuck behind capital controls in two markets." Trapped cash is…
options: cash that has been lost to fraud
cash that cannot easily be moved out of a jurisdiction
cash held in a foreign currency
items.why: Trapped cash = caixa aprisionado: saldos presos onde não podem ser facilmente movimentados.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A large ___ sitting in a low-interest account earns almost nothing and quietly erodes returns."
items.why: Idle balance = saldo ocioso, dinheiro parado que rende pouco e reduz o retorno.

items.q: "With that cash freed, we would have the internal firepower to close the acquisition without borrowing." Firepower here means…
options: the speed of the approval process
the financial capacity to act decisively
items.why: Firepower = poder de fogo: capacidade financeira de agir com força.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A sudden ___ — a bank pulling a credit line overnight — is exactly what the reserve is designed to absorb."
items.why: Funding shock = choque de financiamento: perda súbita de acesso a recursos.

items.q: "After netting intragroup loans, our net position is stronger than the gross figure implies." Net position refers to…
options: the total of all cash accounts added together
the cash held only at head office
the balance after offsetting what is owed against what is held
items.why: Net position = posição líquida: o saldo depois de compensar créditos e débitos internos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em comitês de tesouraria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on releasing the trapped pools." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new pooling structure region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Two country heads pushed back on repatriating the balances." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo, sem necessariamente vetar.

items.q: "The committee endorsed the plan but never followed through on the disbursements." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Freeing one small pool will not move the needle on our overall liquidity." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar diferença perceptível.
